summary: Rabbi Besser explores the tradition of eating dairy on Shabuot, examining various reasons for the custom including the historical context of the giving of the Torah. He emphasizes that the practice serves as a reminder that every person has a unique path to greatness, regardless of their background or lineage. The class encourages listeners to recognize their own potential to achieve their unique purpose in the world.
questions: Why do we eat dairy on Shabuot?
Is it permissible for a Jewish baby to nurse from a non-Jewish woman?
How can everyone be capable of becoming a Tzadik like Moshe?
What does it mean that the world was created for me?
Why does the Torah sometimes omit the names of parents when introducing a person?
